title: Escape velocity: why you can't escape the 9-to-5
hook: You got the raise. So why are you still trapped?

scenes.show: You got the raise. So why are you still trapped?
scenes.say: You got the raise. So why are you still trapped?
Same train. Same desk. Same hope next year is different.
Then you open your phone. Everyone else is winning.

scenes.show: Their car. Their house. Their trip.
scenes.say: Their car. Their house. Their trip. Yours feels small.

scenes.show: The raise buys a life that looks fine.
scenes.say: So every raise buys a life that looks fine. Never a way out.
Every upgrade is another bill. The bigger it looks, the tighter it holds.
Of {n_paths} simulated careers that spent every raise, only {esc_a_n} broke free.

scenes.say: Escape velocity isn't a bigger salary. It's when you stop paying to be seen.

scenes.say: The salary was never the trap. Needing them to see it was.

takeaway: Your salary was never the trap. Needing them to see it was.
cta: Like and follow QuanTik for more dark truths about money
caption:
You got the raise. You're still trapped. Not because you earn too little, but because every raise goes into looking like you're doing fine. We simulated {n_paths} careers that saved {save} and spent every raise: after {years} years, only {esc_a_n} broke free. Escape velocity isn't a bigger salary. It's needing less applause than you earn.

(Simulation: {ret} real return, {vol} volatility, {raise} raises a year, {wr} withdrawal rule, no taxes or fees. An illustration of a mechanism, not a plan.)

claims.text: Trong 2.000 sự nghiệp mô phỏng tiết kiệm 10% và tiêu hết phần tăng lương, chỉ số ít đạt mức thu nhập đầu tư trả đủ chi tiêu sau 40 năm
Quy tắc rút 4%/năm là quy ước từ nghiên cứu dữ liệu lịch sử Mỹ, không phải bảo đảm
